newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel hard hit by crude's drop.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel hard hit by crude's drop.

text.p: European straight-run was hard hit on Wednesday by crude's fall, with prices tumbling but no deals seen done, traders said.
Unhappy sellers quoted offer levels of $105 and $104.50 fob a tonne, some $3-$4 down, but found little interest. Bidders refused to budge above $102-$103.
"The market has turned against us, its very frustrating," said one seller.
The fall came after a deal on Tuesday from an Irish refinery to a major for an 8,000 tonne parcel believed heading to France.
It was heard done on a floating price basis equivalent to around $107 a tonne fob and allowed the seller to move the dates on their next cargo back by several days.
Russian straight-run also suffered from the effect of the fall in crude.
"Refinery economics are now more in favour of crude than residual fuel, so we've backed off," said one buyer. "Supplies are maybe at the same level as last week but the demand has disappeared."
An E-4 from St. Petersburg sold into Antwerp on Tuesday for three means plus $4.25 but the premium was heard to have dropped to $3-$4 today.
